```plato

    //==
    // # Evaluating the named space curves
    //
    // Closed-form evaluation of the space curves declared in `curves-shapes.types.plato`.
    //
    // Conventions:
    //   * The canonical curve parameter is `t` in [0, 1].
    //   * Types carrying an `Angles: AngleInterval` sweep map t through
    //     `Angles.Lerp(t)`; the knots and closed curves map t to `t.Turns`, one
    //     full revolution of their defining parameter.
    //   * Every formula is written in the curve's own frame and placed with
    //     `FramePoint` below, so the declaration comment "winds about the frame's
    //     Z axis" is what the body actually does.
    //
    // TODO(interface-gap): an angular curve whose natural parameter is an `Angle`,
    // bridged by one `Eval(curve, t: Number) => curve.Eval(t.Turns)`, has no
    // counterpart interface here. This is NOT a fold gap; the P2
    // `Reduce`/`MapRange` primitives do not touch it. The clean fix is a
    // `interface IAngularCurve3D` (obligation `Eval(self, theta: Angle): Point3D`)
    // plus one bridge, whose natural home is `curves.concepts.plato`,
    // owned by the curves package and not editable from this library-body pass.
    // Until it lands the `t.Turns` conversion is repeated in each `Eval` below.
    // See the matching note in the spirals section above.

    //==
    // # Shared helpers

    // The point at the given local coordinates of an orthonormal frame:
    // Origin + x*XAxis + y*YAxis + z*ZAxis. Places a curve written in its own
    // canonical position into world space.
    FramePoint(f: Frame3D, x: Number, y: Number, z: Number): Point3D
        => f.Origin + f.XAxis.Vector * x + f.YAxis.Vector * y + f.ZAxis.Vector * z;
```
